content: Materialized rollups vs on-the-fly aggregation for growing time-series data: on-the-fly aggregation over raw rows degrades as data grows (full/linear scans); hybrid approach is standard practice — precompute rollup rows for historical/closed periods (upsert incrementally, never full rebuild), compute on-the-fly only for the small recent/open window, and use multiple granularities (day/week/month) so query cost doesn't scale with history length. For SQLite specifically (no native materialized view/continuous-aggregate support), this means an explicit rollup table maintained by triggers or a scheduled recompute job, not a view.
